title: Delhi saw 11 nights this summer when minimum was above 30 degrees Celsius; it was just 2 last year - The Times of India

full_text:
New Delhi: Delhiites grappled with scorching daytime temperatures, but the nights also offered little relief this summer. An analysis of India Meteorological Department (IMD) data from the past 10 years by
TOI shows that the city’s minimum temperature stayed at or above 30 degrees Celsius on 11 nights this season against two last year.
Instead of cooling down after sunset, temperatures remained unusually high, making sleep difficult and increasing heat stress. While the summer of 2024 recorded 23 nights when the minimum temperature remained above 30 degrees Celsius, the corresponding figures were just one in 2023, six in 2022, three in 2021 and four in 2020. In 2019, it was 12 nights, while 2018 and 2017 witnessed 18 and six such nights.
Of the 11 nights this year, two were in May, four in June and five in July, while 2025 saw two such nights in June. “High minimum temperatures are mostly recorded from May to early July,” said a Met official.
The minimum temperature rises due to two reasons. “When both day and night are hot, heatwave conditions cause a rise in night temperatures. Minimum temperature also increases when it’s cloudy,” said IMD scientist
Krishna Mishra.
IMD’s data shows that the city’s minimum crossed 30 degrees mostly on the same day when the day temperature was above normal.
For instance, out of July’s five nights, four were witnessed from July 16 to 19 when the maximum temperature was in the range of 38-39 degrees Celsius and rain occurred on July 20.
The city saw 11 nights when minimum temperatures were 30 degrees Celsius, but only one night met the ‘warm night’ condition. IMD considers a ‘warm night’ when the maximum temperature is over 40 degrees Celsius and the departure of minimum temperature is 4.5 degrees Celsius or more above normal.
The season’s only warm night was on May 21 when the minimum temperature at base station Safdarjung settled at 31.9 degrees Celsius, 5.2 degrees above normal. It was also the warmest May night in Delhi in 14 years, according to IMD data.
Rain brings slight reliefParts of Delhi recorded light to moderate showers Monday afternoon, bringing respite from soaring mercury. IMD has issued a yellow alert for moderate rain Tuesday and Wednesday.
Earlier, Delhiites experienced hot and humid conditions, with the heat index, staying at 48 degrees Celsius for the second consecutive day. The maximum temperature was 38.1 degrees Celsius, three degrees above normal. The minimum was 28.6 degrees Celsius, one degree above normal.
From 2.30pm to 5.30pm, Safdarjung logged 8mm of rainfall, while Ridge in north Delhi and Lodhi Road recorded 19.4mm and 11.5mm.
